issues.description: generate-stories cannot bootstrap a fresh repo because it requires an existing data/stories/manifest.json for topics.
The configured story dataset is absent, so make demo / emovec all cannot run from a clean checkout.
from_pretrained uses dtype= while the declared transformers lower bound includes versions expecting torch_dtype=.
Saved vector artifacts are loaded without validating manifest model, scale, layer count, hidden size, or emotion compatibility.
Emotion names from config are used directly as directory names, allowing path traversal or invalid filesystem paths.
Emotion names are interpolated directly into output filenames, allowing path traversal or broken filenames.
Outbound story generation has no timeout, retry, status validation, or partial-run recovery, so it can hang or leave corrupt datasets.
Config values are coerced but not validated, so invalid PCA targets, layer ranges, batch sizes, dtypes, or scale counts fail late and opaquely.
Very short tokenized texts can produce L == s and divide by zero during mean activation weighting.
PCA on zero-variance or degenerate activation matrices divides by zero and can return NaN components.
all_token_activations stacks every hidden state for each batch on CPU, creating large avoidable memory spikes.
choice_logits ignores small configured batch sizes by forcing batches of at least 8, risking OOM on constrained devices.
load_stories ignores the dataset manifest and does not verify that the on-disk corpus matches the configured emotions/topics/counts.
Logit-lens tokens and emotion labels are written into markdown table cells without escaping pipes or newlines.
Output directories are reused without cleaning or run IDs, making stale artifacts easy to mix with fresh results.
Generated packaging metadata is checked into the source tree.
Generated experiment outputs and binary arrays are present in the repo, adding stale state and about 14 MB of noise.
Dependencies are broad lower bounds with no lockfile, making ML/runtime behavior non-reproducible across machines.
